doc.title: Butch Cage and Robert Pete Williams Interview, 1967-05-13
doc.interviewee: Butch Cage and Robert Pete Williams

chapter: Williams on guitarists, family and touring
title: Harmonica players and Williams giving up harmonica
summary: They discuss a young harmonica player; Williams says he used to play harmonica until his tonsils got bad and gave one away to Junior Welch.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: I know that used to play with Smokey Babe on the record. Where did you want? Well, anyhow. Oh, is that guy a young student that played the Harmonica? I'm trying to remember now. Well, they had him over here at the LSU too when he was out there blowing his Harmonita too. I'm trying to remember who that is. Do you remember? I don't remember who that is. Do you remember? I don't remember. I don't remember. I don't remember. I don't remember. I don't remember.
I don't remember. Well, he's a little bit heavier than I am.
It may not be as heavy.
But that's all he plays is a harmonita. A young man? Yes, he's young. He's very good with that harmonita.
Yes, I used to play harmonica a great bit before my tonsils got too bad.

I used to play a harmonica a great bit before my tonsils got too bad. Couldn't play it now. And I've been thinking about just going, give me a rack, and put my music in with a harmonica to save me a singing, you know. Every once in a while I sing. So that's what I'm figuring on down. I had a harmonica when I was over in Los Angeles. No, not there I was. Yeah. I was in Los Angeles. I believe it was. See, now I don't want to get it. I was. But Junior Welch, he wanted it, and I let him have it. Yes. Joe Turner, he lives in New Orleans too. He was overseas with us.
